title: Chrome 155 Fixes Critical Prerender Flaw, Nine Other Security Bugs
excerpt: Google's October 15 Stable update patches CVE-2026-110922 and nine other flaws in builds 155.0.8059.84/.85 — update via About Chrome and relaunch to install it.
body:
• Google's October 15 Chrome 155 Stable update fixes 10 security flaws: one Critical, six High and three Medium severity.
  • The Critical flaw, CVE-2026-110922, is a use-after-free bug in Prerender, reported by Xinyang Ge on October 2; patched builds are 155.0.8059.84/.85 for Windows and Mac and 155.0.8059.84 for Linux.
  • One High flaw, CVE-2026-110913 in DOM, was reported by Xinyang Ge of Anthropic assisted by Claude, an AI credit listed in Google's advisory.
  • To update now: open Chrome's About page via Settings or chrome://settings/help, let it download, then relaunch — Google reports no exploitation in the wild for this batch, but details stay restricted until most users update.

Google has released a Chrome 155 Stable channel update fixing 10 security vulnerabilities, including a Critical use-after-free flaw in the browser's Prerender feature, according to GBHackers. The update, published on October 15, 2026, moves Chrome to version 155.0.8059.84/.85 for Windows and Mac and 155.0.8059.84 for Linux, rolling out over the coming days and weeks.

Users do not need to wait for the automatic rollout. Opening Chrome's About page triggers a check, and a relaunch completes the install — the action Google and security advisories recommend for a Critical memory flaw.

The Critical flaw: CVE-2026-110922

The most serious bug is CVE-2026-110922, a use-after-free vulnerability in Prerender, the feature that loads pages in the background to speed up navigation. Researcher Xinyang Ge reported it on October 2, 2026, according to the Chrome Releases advisory.

Use-after-free bugs occur when code continues to use memory after it has been freed. Attackers who can trigger such a flaw can corrupt memory and, in some cases, achieve arbitrary code execution inside the browser renderer. Google has not published exploitation details for this bug, and the advisory does not report exploitation in the wild. As is standard, Google keeps bug-tracker access restricted until a majority of users have updated.

The other nine fixes

Six flaws are rated High. They include CVE-2026-110913, a memory corruption issue in DOM; CVE-2026-110919 and CVE-2026-110921, use-after-free flaws in V8, Chrome's JavaScript and WebAssembly engine; CVE-2026-110920, a memory corruption flaw also in V8; CVE-2026-110918, a memory corruption flaw in Core; and CVE-2026-110917, a memory corruption flaw in SVG reported by researcher C0rk1. Xinyang Ge reported four of the High-severity flaws.

CVE-2026-110913 stands out for how it was found. Google credits it to Xinyang Ge of Anthropic, assisted by Claude, reported on September 29, 2026, Cyber Security News noted. The credit reflects a growing pattern of AI-assisted vulnerability research appearing in vendor advisories, though Google's note does not describe what role the model played in finding or analysing the flaw.

The three Medium-severity fixes, all reported by Google, are CVE-2026-110916, an improper input validation flaw in Desktop, reported as early as April 12, 2026; CVE-2026-110915, a use-after-free flaw in Compositing; and CVE-2026-110914, a memory corruption flaw in Workers. Google says many bugs in the release were found with tools including AddressSanitizer, MemorySanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, Control Flow Integrity, libFuzzer and AFL.

Context: a busy month for Chrome patches

This 10-fix update is the latest in a series of Chrome 155 security releases, not the whole of Chrome 155. Earlier Chrome 155 Stable updates addressed larger batches of vulnerabilities. That distinction matters for readers checking coverage: being on an early 155 build is not the same as being on 155.0.8059.84 or .85. The version number, not just the major release, is what shows whether this Prerender fix is installed.

Other Chromium-based browsers such as Microsoft Edge, Brave and Opera often inherit the same underlying fixes, GBHackers noted, but each vendor ships its own patched release on its own schedule. Checking Chrome alone does not confirm those browsers are updated.

What readers should do

On desktop, open Chrome, go to Settings and About Chrome — or type chrome://settings/help in the address bar — wait for version 155.0.8059.84/.85 to download, and click Relaunch. On managed work or school devices, administrators should push the patched build across the fleet and confirm browsers actually restart, since a downloaded update does not protect a browser that keeps running the old version.

Google has given no reason to treat this as an actively exploited emergency, and it has reported no in-the-wild exploitation for this batch. The reason to update promptly is simpler: a Critical use-after-free in a feature that preloads web pages is exactly the class of bug attackers study once a patch makes its location public. Updating closes that window.
